utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Stojanovic, may I take it that you do not oppose that a copy of the chart will be given to the witness and that I give the instructions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, but I would also like it if we were to receive a copy of the chart so that we can look it -- look at it as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has it not been provided yet without the English version, first of all, to the Prosecution, Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I just received it, and I showed it to Mr. Stojanovic just now. I'm preparing to send him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was a copy --

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The English version has been made available earlier, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Stojanovic, you have both copies now so some homework to be done for the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please continue and see if we can conclude today.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Since I will be using P738, with your leave, I would like to ask that the witness be given a copy of the statement that we will be using. This is a redacted version. But just in case, for the sake of caution, we would prefer this to be under seal. This is P738, the B/C/S version, statement made on the 19th and 20th of April, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is already in evidence. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I wanted to go through your statement and to get some clarifications from you, and I also would like us to be careful when mentioning names. You say that before the war broke out, you were a member of the Main Board of the SDA. What I would like to know is what your specific duties were?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I didn't have any particular duties other than that I was a member of the local organisation of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And how many people were there in the Main Board at the time?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: In the beginning there were 12. Later it expanded to 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you take part in talks about the division of power in the municipality where you come from?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No, not directly. I was a member of a commission for the appointment to posts, but these negotiations actually never took part because the Serb side would always find some reason to postpone this discussion. They simply were not interested in appointing certain cadres to the posts signed to the Muslims or to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And the meetings that you attended, was there any discussion about the arming of the Bosniak population?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No, because we still had a lot of confidence in the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you know anything about the distribution of weapons and military equipment according to ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You were brought in on the 11th of April, 1992. Is that the correct date?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, I was not taken in. I was captured. There is a difference between being taken in or brought in and being captured. My hands were tied at the place where I worked, where I used to work for 25 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And who did that?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: This was done by people unknown to me. These were actually members of the JNA who told me and my director and the drivers -- they tied our hands, actually. But Serbs familiar to me helped them. They entered the medical centre earlier, sometime before noon. They were armed with infantry weapons and 48s and Kalashnikovs. They were dressed in former JNA uniforms. The unit was under the command of Radomir Cicmil, aka Cile. He had the rank of captain. He introduced himself to us as being in charge of that squad. There were some 10 to 12 people there -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most of all this is in the name of the statement. The name of the commander, that he knew some of them, how they came. Mr. Stojanovic, could you please put focused questions on relevant issues and especially issues that you wish to challenge. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I did not ask this of the witness. The question was much simpler, but the witness just continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let's try to focus on what my questions are specifically. This arrest and capture, according to you, does that have anything to do with your political activities?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No, no. It was just that I was a Muslim and that I was in favour of a different option.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say a different option, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't in the SDS, but I was in the SDA, and the option implied reasonable life together with neighbours and Serbs. It did not include preparations for war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So I would be right if I were to say that this capture of yours directly had to do with your political engagement in the Party for Democratic Action; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No. No. How can you get that out of it if I said that the capture was the result of my being a Muslim and that I belonged to a different option? Perhaps you can take it in that context a little bit, but not absolutely as the decisive factor. It had nothing to do with it that I was a member of the SDA, because it didn't bother me that all the Serbs were in the SDS and that there was an organisation where they could come together and agree on what to do. There were more Muslims than Serbs in Foca, and it never bothered me personally that an organisation existed that would gather each ethnic group where they would sit and discuss their life and goings-on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question has been answered. Mr. Stojanovic, I think you could have concluded that five lines ago as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, were there political options where you were from that did not have any national or ethnic qualifiers?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes. There were several. There were reformists in favour of Yugoslavia. This was the party of Ante Markovic. There were also Communists. It wasn't a significant number, but they did have a representative each in the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After you spent five days at Livade, you were transferred to the KP Dom Foca?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this: When you came, can you remember who the warden was of KP Dom in Foca?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I was transferred from Livade on the 17th, late at night, and then the following day on the 18th I learned that the camp commander was Milorad Krnojelac. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And are you able to tell us if you know who was the KP Foca warden before Milorad Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes. This was Radojica Tesovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 65 ter document 11167 in e-court, please. The document is not under seal, Your Honours. Sir, according to your best recollection, who was charge of KP Foca at the time? Which jurisdiction was it under?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: It was under the jurisdiction of the SDS or the Territorial Defence of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can we agree that it was a correctional facility where convicts throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina would serve their long prison sentences, and they came from all other Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm also addressing you, Mr. Groome. Is there any dispute about Mr. Krnojelac being the warden and being appointed by the minister of justice in, say, the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: No dispute, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then they are useless questions apart from that part of it is already in the statement. Mr. Stojanovic, could I really urge you to immediately move to matters in dispute and relevant to the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Then I would just like to tender this document 11167.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although agreed upon. No objections I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D133, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed to relevant and disputed issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you please tell us if the guards in KP Dom were employees of the justice ministry?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: The KP Dom staff, specifically the guards, were working there from before. I assume that they were appointed by the commander, the camp commander, Mr. Krnojelac, to their duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can we agree that these were not members of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No, but members of the Army of Republika Srpska in the beginning frequently would come in, enter the rooms. They would search us, and this went on for some 10 or 15 days after the arrest of the Muslims from Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you about that as well. Can you please just answer my questions. So the staff at the KP Dom were not members of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. But actually I must correct myself. For 15 days they did carry out these duties that we discussed, and they were wearing these uniforms that were well known to me, blue uniforms, but then for the subsequent 15 days they would go to the front throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina and then they would probably be wearing proper military uniforms. We found out this from the work platoons, because some 40 to 50 people would leave every day to work on the farms or in some other work units that the KP Dom had even before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After you came to the KP Dom on the 17th of April, you said that for the first 15 days soldiers did come. Can you please tell us what they did there.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: They conducted searches. They confiscated jewellery. They abused people. In that period there was a group of guards from Uzice as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can we agree that this is the period before the Army of Republika Srpska was formed that was still during the time of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: That means that I am speaking the truth, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. Do we agree that this was during the period when the JNA still existed and that this was the period when the Army of Republika Srpska was still not formed?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes. The Army of Republika Srpska was officially formed on the 12th of May, 1992. Up until then, there was the Territorial Defence which actually transformed into the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at 65 ter document 08444. This document needn't be under seal either, Your Honour. The date is the 18th of June, 1992. As you can see on the next page, it was signed by the War Presidency president, Miroslav Stanic. In the third paragraph of the document it reads: "The current military and civilian authorities of the Serbian municipality of Foca have thus far forbidden to both groups to leave the territory of Foca municipality. It is quite normal that any family would like to and want to live together. That is why it comes as no surprise that there is ever-increasing pressure on the military and civilian authorities. In item 1 the document states: "The civilian and military authorities shall allow all loyal citizens who have not violated the laws of the BH Serbian Republic or done anything in this still-ongoing bar to endanger the safety of the Serbian people in our area to leave in the direction of their choice." Do you have any knowledge about this document and the issues discussed therein?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: This is simply not true. They did not allow Muslims to leave the town of Foca of their own free will. This is nebulous, drafted by Commander Stanic whom I knew personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In June 1992, was there freedom of movement for the entire population of Foca municipality by that time?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No. No. Please allow me to clarify. As soon as conflicts broke out, most of the able-bodied men were arrested or captured and taken to the KP Dom in Foca. That was in town. While some of them managed to flee in the direction of Trnovo. In the town itself, what was left was basically the elderly, women, and children. Whoever was able to escape that hell had to cross the Drina, which had very high levels at that time of year, but people were prepared to do anything to escape the hell of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you have such knowledge, could you tell us whether parts of Foca municipality were controlled by members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No, because by that time that army had not been formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the existence of certain elements of the Patriotic League in the territory of Foca municipality at the time?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in the general area of Foca municipality, in the direction of Gorazde and Tjentiste at the time there was combat?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes. At the foot of the hills in the direction of those places there was some combat, especially in the direction of Gorazde. All able-bodied men from Foca were engaged in defending Gorazde straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Ustikolina, who controlled it at the time?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: On the 26th of April, it was taken over by Serb forces, and they continued further afield to Osanice, which is some 20 kilometres away. They were stopped there. Throughout the war the line remained the same. There were no movements any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the first several months of your stay in KP Foca, were there any captured members of the Bosniak army, the TO, the Patriotic League, the Green Berets, or later the Army of BH?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No. Everyone who was there was civilian. If anyone happened to be captured at the front lines who belonged to the Muslim side, they were never brought in there. They were liquidated right there and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How would you know that?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Well, I do. If I were to describe Bosnia-Herzegovina as a large patchwork, within that patchwork Foca was but a piece. But the worst things happened there with regards to people and property.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you how you know that such people were killed on the spot when captured. Did you have occasion to see that?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I didn't have occasion to see soldiers killing someone like that, but later on when I was exchanged, I learned that such things happened, and such soldiers who were killed in that way were then used by the Serb side to have exchanges of the killed. There was such practice in place throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina. The sides exchanged their dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question was this: Did you have any direct knowledge in order for you to be able to assert that soldiers were not being captured?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: There were no captured soldiers who were brought to the KP Dom in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay in the KP Dom in Foca were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes, twice. The interrogation was carried out by Zoran Vladic whom I knew personally. He used to be a scene of crime officer with the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I read from the witness statement: "I was interrogated twice during my time in KP Dom." What is the use of asking whether he was interrogated unless you have serious reasons to challenge that? That's -- it's not here to hear the story again. It is -- you are expected to cross-examine the witness on the evidence he has given. Would you please do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will rely on this precisely because of the people who took statements from this witness. That is why I simply wanted the witness to confirm. I do not dispute what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you the following: Save for the gentleman you mentioned, who else interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No one else did, but I was captured and taken to a solitary cell in building number one on the third evening. I spent there four days and four nights. The people involved were guardsmen and the prison guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try again. My question is this: Please tell the Court what you were interrogated about.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: He wanted to know where I was before my capture, where I moved, whether I possessed any weapons, and that was it. Mr. Vladic knew me all too well, and they found nothing in my apartment. I had no reason to be concerned about such an interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign any kind of statement?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes, I had to. It was customary to have such statements signed, because the interrogator would require that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You were interrogated by the employees of the KP Dom, not by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes. I think at the time they were designated to those positions, and they were in charge of interrogating or, as they called it, processing detainees. There was Mr. Koprivica and then someone known as Miso as well as Vojo Starovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to those men, do you know whether anybody else interrogated detainees during your stay in the KP Dom in Foca?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes. There was a room used for torture, if I may say so. That's where military policemen came at first, and they interrogated and tortured prisoners who came after I did, and they told me what kind of torture they had been put through.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You did not see that?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I didn't. One couldn't see through walls. But if you have someone who had lived through such torture come to your cell and they tell you about it and I can see numerous bruises caused by blunt instruments, then of course it tells me that it was indeed done.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Except for the occasion when you were brought to the KP Dom in Foca, otherwise you were not beaten.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I was. There was a guardsman who hit me with the baton on the back. Another one came and slapped me around as well. Standing next to us were the policemen, Serb guards, who did not stop that. Following that I was taken to the solitary cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From that moment on until the 5th of July, 1993, when you were transferred to the KP Kula facility, you were not further abused or beaten?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I was not physically mistreated, but I was mistreated in other ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to assist the people (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Only in the presence of policemen, when Gojko Jokanovic, the nurse, allowed or requested for it to be done. He wasn't qualified to administer any kind of aid. There had been a physician, a doctor, but as of March he had fled Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay in KP Foca, you received three meals a day; correct?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes. But it was enough to keep you alive, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How were you accommodated? Were there any beds?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the previous question. The statement reads, "We were fed regularly this whole time at KP Dom." Therefore, you're seeking, apart from that the answer might not only favour your case but there's no need to ask again what is already clearly in the statement, and I waited until your next question to know for sure that there was no follow-up. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I will abide by your instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The food you were given, can you tell the Court where it was prepared and cooked and then given to you?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes. It was in front of the restaurant where they had a trellis, and they had large cauldrons where food was prepared for the detainees, and in the mess itself it was served upon us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The food was not prepared by the army, it was prepared by the management and staff of the KP Dom in Foca; correct?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to discuss Mr. Kovac you mentioned. I wanted to draw your attention to paragraph -- the first paragraph on page 8 in the B/C/S, which is paragraph 45. At least that's how I marked it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English, Your Honour, it is page 8, the fourth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you can find it in your hard copy.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Which page?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version, it is page 8, the first paragraph. Let me ask you this: What is your knowledge concerning the man whom you knew as Commander Kovac?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I know he had been an officer with the former JNA before the war and that his rank was that of captain. The Foca SDS invited him and another 11 officers to take part in the war effort against Muslims. He was appointed as one of the senior commanders of what was to become the Foca Brigade. At first it was called the Foca Tactical Group or the Drina group. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to see him there?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No, I did not, but he was well described to me by the Cengic cousins. They told me he was short, very strict, and in conversation with the three of them, he told them that now was the right time to settle accounts with Muslims and that Muslims would never live in Foca again, that it was Serbian land. He also told them that he was sorry to have them transported to Belgrade. It was in January 1993, and the conversation took place in the camp warden's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't attend the conversation?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I did not, but the words were conveyed to me by the people I trust to the fullest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness said that he never had occasion to see him, how could he possibly attend a conversation between the source of his knowledge and the person involved? And if you look at the statement, you see that the person is described as a short person. I wouldn't need that description if I would have seen the person. So, Mr. Stojanovic, please do what you're expected to do in the interest of your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I just wanted to finish with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Everything that you've just said in relation to Mr. Kovac is information that you got from other people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the answer to the previous question, "I did not attend, but the words were conveyed." He has never seen the person, and he describes what information was given about a conversation these other people had. Superfluous question. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the paragraph that I showed you, you say, in describing Kovac in the same way: "They talked with him at the KP Dom sometime in April 1993." Please, who was it that talked in April?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there was a correction made. It is the 15th of January, actually, because in previous documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then when you say "they," you mean the gentleman that you mentioned just a bit earlier?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you say: "After my complaints, there were some slight changes." Who did you address your complaints to?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: In order improve the situation for the inmates.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To whom did you address those complaints, because that was the question put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were objections made to the warden on two occasions when seeing him that he could do something to improve the situation, and also there was a complaint addressed to the deputy of the council.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the name you mentioned, the deputy of the council. Did you give a name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His name was Savo Todovic, Todovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you said that after my complaints there was some slight changes, what happened? What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Well, after a month or two they gave us another small slice of bread. That's what the use was of that conversation. But I think that that was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you speak with Mr. Todovic or with Mr. Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: With both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me who did you talk about regarding your exchange?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: You mean at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the Foca KP Dom, before you left for Kula.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I spoke with the warden, Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Kovac, whom you mentioned, had nothing to do with your status or with your exchange; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Well, I really couldn't rule that out or I couldn't confirm it, because he was the superior of the civilian affairs sector at the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the Chamber has considered the development of the cross-examination. We unfortunately had to establish that the majority of your questions find already a relatively precise answer in the statement. You asked him, for example, the last, did you speak to Mr. Todovic and Mr. Krnojelac. That's in the second statement. It's clear that the witness spoke with them. That's -- I would say 70 per cent of your questions are related to matters which are already in the statement despite the fact that we invited you again and again not to do that. We approach the matter differently. During the next break, you'll have an opportunity, apart from looking at the chart, you have an opportunity to review your questions against the statements which were tendered by the Prosecution and which were admitted. Then you have another 15 minutes to put questions to the witness and that is it. Meanwhile, we'll invite the witness, Witness RM046, a translation in your own language of a chart is available now. We'd like you to carefully read during the next break that chart and your comments. What we're interested to know at the end is whether it reflects accurately your comments and whether the comments are true to the best of your knowledge. We'd like to hear that from you after the break. If you would please be so kind as to do that. Then we current into closed session in order for you to be able to leave the courtroom, and the chart will be handed out to you -- Mr. Stojanovic, would you still wish to inspect the chart as given to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I will also look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, at this moment you're invited to look at whether this is -- whether you have any objection against this to be given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The chart is handed out to you now. We move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Stojanovic, you have time until 10 minutes past 2.00. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to put just a few things to you, and I would like you to look at paragraph 43 of your statement. This is page 7, the one paragraph but last in the B/C/S, and then in the English it's page 2, the second paragraph. And now you are looking at the list. I would like you to actually look at your statement, sir.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: My pages are not numbered, so can you please tell me exactly which number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I think that you're looking at the list you received just before the break, not at your statement.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that I received it. I have the previous statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Well, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 7, the penultimate paragraph in the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, did you say that we must look at page 2 in the English?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps it's the interpretation. It's page 8, paragraph 2 on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, what I would like to ask you about the forced labour is this: Did you ever have information where the prisoners were taken outside to work, outside of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes. They went to the farm, and they did all the farming work. There was some cattle there, pigs, cows, poultry, and that's the sort of work that they did. Others went to chop wood during the winter. When the weather was quite bad they would collect firewood both for the needs of the KP Dom in order to prepare food, but not for our heating, however. They also collected wood for some citizens of Foca. In the summer they went to cut the grass in the meadows, to collect hay. They did all kinds of physical labour, physical jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And the work that they did, they did it for the KP Dom administration. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Also when they worked at the metal processing factory or the furniture factory within the prison compound, these were facilities that existed from before the war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you say the furniture factory within the prison compound. I see some in the furniture factory and other areas outside the prison. So I'm a bit confused there. Unless I missed a correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Perhaps I was hurrying. I'm familiar with that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you please explain where the physical location of the facility for the manufacture of furniture is?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: It's just outside of the wall of the KP Dom, but there was another perimeter that actually went and included the furniture factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So it would be correct to say that it was part of the overall KP Dom facility?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at paragraph 37 together. This is the last paragraph in pages 6 to 7 in the B/C/S version, and in the English version this is page 7, the third paragraph. My question to you is this: Do you know what the problem was that the Serbs had around the 7th of September? You talk about that in this part of your report.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Should I clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to ask you to do that.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I can see that there was a group of 45 people here taken out on the 17th of September, and there was a serious incident for the Army of Republika Srpska on the 7th of September while transporting weapons from Kalinovik to Foca in order to secure the Foca Brigade. There was a serious incident that occurred when all the weapons were lost and there were casualties. All the personnel died.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me how they died?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Since the Serbs had a vast arsenal of explosive devices and mines, they were placing them everywhere without marking the maps properly, and as the column of vehicles came by with the vehicles and the personnel, they encountered a mine, and there was a pile-up, an accident, and it all went up and turned to ashes. And I just want to add this for the sake of the Chamber: This occurred not far from the village of Ratine, which is in the Foca municipality area, and on the 5th of August, a little bit earlier, the Serbs brought from Kalinovik, from Jelisejsko Polje 24 men --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there. The question was to tell the Chamber how they died, and you have done that. Mr. Stojanovic is limited in his time. Please, next question, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us try and stay focused on what I am asking you about. Let us go back to one detail. Where did you get that information that it occurred due to a landmine planted by the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Nezir Cengic was in the medical centre at the time. He had had a heart infarction. He was there at the time. He saw many coffins in front of the building, and later on when we met he told me everything in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he also tell you that it happened because of a landmine planted by the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes, because the nurses and medical staff were discussing it. That's how he knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us something about the KP Dom Kula where you were transferred on the 5th of July, 1993. Under whose competence was it?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: It was controlled by civilian organs. However, they had superior military structures following the same system that existed in Foca, in Batkovic, and elsewhere in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any kind of operational information that KP Kula was under military authority?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What were conditions like in KP Kula as opposed to Foca?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Pretty much the same. We were on the ground floor where there was a lot of moisture, and there were poor hygiene conditions, much like in Foca. The same goes for medical check-ups. It was very difficult to see a physician. There were always guards there as an obstacle who created problems for us to see doctors. On occasion in the evening when we thought things were better, perhaps we could place a very sick young person on a chair and carry him to the infirmary because he was a severe diabetic. It just so happened that the next day he died.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else. The place Rataj [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic's microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The village of Rataj, which is where you mentioned the VRS soldiers were killed, was it deep inside VRS territory?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Sorry, it wasn't Rataj but Ratine. Yes, it is a village bordering on Foca and Kalinovik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: There was no combat there at the time?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No. It was in September. All of the forces and personnel on the Muslim side had left Foca long ago. In Velibor Ostojic's report, he said that Foca fell on the 26th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your view or as you say in the statement, the ideologists entire -- behind the entire situation there were Ostojic and another person. Who were they?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: They were elected representatives of the Serb people in the BH parliament. Velibor Ostojic was the information minister, and Maksimovic, who used to be a Serbo-Croatian professor at the school of humanities, was appointed SDS club president in the BH parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In that period in 1992 and 1993, they were not part of the military; correct?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: I'm not certain about that. I don't think they were military. Let me add this: But they were tasked with preparing the Serbs for war in Foca, and they were tasked by the BH SDS Main Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you get that information?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: From various sources. I even heard it over the radio. Until the 15th of August we could hear various radio stations, and we could hear both of them speak on Radio Foca in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let us not go into the names of towns, but tell me, was your property returned to you?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Only partially. Let me explain. All that was left were the walls of the apartment. There was no furniture or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you renovate and reconstruct your housing unit?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two minutes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for the two minutes, but I conclude with this question, and I'd like to thank the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Ms. Harbour, perhaps we first deal with the chart, but perhaps first I ask the witness. Were you able to read the chart and your comments in it, Witness RM046?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any need to correct anything as you found it in the chart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I just wanted to add that I was quite pleased to have been able to create this document. I owe you a clarification. Perhaps you will ask yourselves how come I am aware of so much information about every single person. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not seeking such clarification. We take it that you gave your comments to the best of your abilities and on the basis of your experience and knowledge of the circumstances at the time. We accept that. Then, Ms. Harbour, is there any --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I should just add that in the Foca and Kula camp, I spent over 700 days changing cells, and I kept running into other people who always acquainted me with the situation, where they were, where they had worked, et cetera, and that's where much of my information came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment there seems to be no challenge to the source of your information. Ms. Harbour, any need to put further questions to the witness? I note in relation to that that, of course, re-examination is supposed to deal with matters which arise from cross-examination. Well, cross-examination, 90 per cent of what was raised was already in evidence. There might not be much, but if there are any further questions apart from tendering the chart, please put them to the witness and tell us whether you need more than two or three minutes for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no need for redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you deal with the chart.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I will just deal with the chart. Could we please have 65 ter 28654 on the screen. And this would be tendered under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Witness RM046, did you provide this list of names during proofing and provide comments about them?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: As the Chamber has already asked you, did you have an opportunity to review all of the comments that you provided?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Did you identify any material corrections that should be made?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And is this document on the screen before you the same document that you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, no objections? You have had an opportunity to look at it during the break. No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P747, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P747 is admitted under seal. No further questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Moloto may have a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just to ask, you referred to a KOS officer. What is a KOS officer?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: A KOS officer is someone belonging to the JNA, a member of their counter-intelligence service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: Before registering me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Moloto just wanted to know what KOS stood for. Mr. Mladic, you have an opportunity to consult. One second, because it's the very end of the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, just one question stemming from Judge Moloto's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question of Judge Moloto was limited to what KOS meant, not more, nothing less. If you have a question in relation to that, you may put it to the witness. You're not supposed to further explore whether there were KOS officers, et cetera, which you could have done during cross-examination if you had wished to do so. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is this: Do you know the name of this person?

utterances.speaker: RM046
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness RM046, this concludes your evidence. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, questions either raised by the parties or by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. We'll first turn into closed session, but I already announce, since we are now still in open session, that once we are in closed session, that we will adjourn for the day and that we will resume Monday, the 21st of January, at 9.30 in the morning. I think in the same Courtroom I, but at least in the premises of this Tribunal. Courtroom III. I apologise.
